subject: Soft-commit cadence and escrow approach for onboarding
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Simon Park <simon@dataedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Jul 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Soft-commit cadence and escrow approach for onboarding

Hi Simon —

Thanks again for the time yesterday. Per our conversation I attached a short MAP and a proposed commit schedule that favors a soft-commit cadence: an initial low committed TPM in month 1 that steps up monthly based on adoption signals. Key points in the attached: bullets for clarity
- Month 1: 200k TPM (soft commit) + 30k escrow credit to cover early overage protection
- Months 2–4: 400k / 700k / 1.0M TPM targets (hardening to firm commit by month 4)
- Discounts: staged volume discounts that kick in when a monthly threshold is hit three times in a rolling 3-month window

Question for you: would DataEdge accept an escrow mechanism where a pre-funded credit (held in escrow) is drawn down only if committed volumes are missed, and is otherwise refunded or applied to month 1 usage? We proposed a refundable escrow to reduce downside for your team while giving us predictable runway to provision Dedicated capacity if needed.

I attached: DataEdge_Redwood_MAP_v1.2.pdf and DE-8421_commit_schedule.xlsx

Next steps if that looks okay: 1) Simon approves the sash (MAP) and cadence, 2) we convert the MAP into a short SOW and route to Legal/Procurement, 3) DocuSign signature and escrow transfer.

Thanks,
Marcus Lin
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.com
+1 (415) 555-0187
From: Simon Park <simon@dataedge.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Reddy <priya@dataedge.ai>
Date: Tue, 14 Jul 2026 14:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Soft-commit cadence and escrow approach for onboarding

Marcus —

Appreciate the clear summary and attachments. A couple quick items from our side: we like the staged discounts but have two asks before we move to Legal/Procurement.

1) Escrow mechanics: we prefer the escrow to be a true pre-fund that can be consumed as committed usage rather than a separate hold. That means if month 1 usage <= committed, escrow is applied to next month; if usage > committed and we under-deliver later, Redwood draws from escrow to cover the delta. We want clarity on refund timing and any fees.

2) Soft-commit floor: can we set a minimum monthly floor of 150k TPM (instead of 200k) in month 1, with a clear path to 1.0M by month 4 tied to three adoption metrics (active users, inference calls/day, and model latency < 500ms)? If those metrics meet the gating criteria we can convert to firm commit earlier.

Also CC'ing Priya (our product lead) — she will validate the adoption metrics.

On escrow fees / timelines: what is Redwood's standard process for refunding remaining escrow if we accelerate and the amount is no longer needed?

Thanks,
Simon
Head of AI Platforms | DataEdge
simon@dataedge.ai
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Simon Park <simon@dataedge.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 16 Jul 2026 10:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Soft-commit cadence and escrow approach for onboarding

Simon — quick follow-up from Legal/Finance side (looping in from our end):

Thanks for the clear asks. A few clarifications to make sure Procurement will greenlight this quickly:

- Escrow structure: Redwood proposes a custodial escrow account managed by our payments partner. Practical flow: DataEdge wires escrow to the escrow account prior to SOW signature; escrow is earmarked for DE-8421. Monthly, usage is invoiced and we first apply escrow to any overages against committed thresholds. Any unused escrow at contract termination or after a mutually agreed acceleration is refunded within 14 business days, minus any consumed overages. No escrow management fee for the first 90 days — after that a nominal fee applies (we can bury this in SOW if needed).

- Minimum floor: We are fine moving month 1 floor to 150k TPM. To accelerate to firm commit early we will use the three adoption metrics you suggested. We will include a simple attestation process where DataEdge's product lead confirms the metrics and Redwood validates telemetry for the period.

- Discounts: Example ladder included in the spreadsheet: 3% at 300k TPM, 7% at 700k TPM, 12% at 1.0M+. Discounts apply to billed tokens for the month where threshold achieved and retroactive adjustments are made if thresholds are met for the rolling-window conditions described.

I'll add a short paragraph to the MAP PDF clarifying refund and fee timing and will version to v1.3 if you want to proceed.

—Marissa
Director, Commercial Operations | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>
To: Simon Park <simon@dataedge.ai>, Priya Reddy <priya@dataedge.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:47:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Soft-commit cadence and escrow approach for onboarding

Simon / Priya —

Great — thanks for the quick feedback. Summary of agreed adjustments and next steps (short bullets):
- Month 1 floor: 150k TPM (soft commit).
- Escrow: pre-funded custodial account; refunded within 14 business days after acceleration/termination; no management fee first 90 days.
- Ramp: Month 2 = 400k, Month 3 = 700k, Month 4 = 1.0M TPM (targets in spreadsheet).
- Discounts: 3% @ 300k, 7% @ 700k, 12% @ 1.0M (retroactivity rules as Marissa described).
- Acceleration path: achievement of three adoption metrics triggers early conversion to firm commit — Priya to attest, Redwood to validate via telemetry.

If that aligns with your internal approvals, I'll push v1.3 of the MAP and the short SOW to DocuSign this afternoon. Requested action: can you confirm procurement/finance are OK with the escrow timing and we have a sign-off contact for the DocuSign?

Thanks — excited to get you onboarded.

Marcus
